intro: Same kaam ko fast aur readable banane wale tools: comprehensions, generators, zip/enumerate, Counter/defaultdict/deque aur functools. Is section ka focus hai sahi data structure chunna aur memory waste kiye bina iteration karna.
theory: List comprehension loop se chhoti aur tez hoti hai, par usme side effects ya bahut complicated logic nahi hona chahiye — tab normal loop zyada readable hai.
Generator values ko lazily deta hai, isliye poori list memory me nahi banti. Bade files/streams ke liye generator expression ya `yield` use karo.
enumerate index aur value dono deta hai; zip do ya zyada iterables ko parallel chalata hai. Manual range(len(...)) se ye dono behtar hain.
collections ke specialised containers: Counter ginti, defaultdict default values, deque fast append/pop dono ends par.
functools.lru_cache pure functions ke repeated calls cache karta hai; `sum(x*x for x in data)` jaisa generator built-in ko de sakte ho.
syntax:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque
counts = Counter(words)
groups = defaultdict(list)
queue = deque([1, 2, 3])
queue.appendleft(0)

examples.code:
from collections import Counter

words = ['sql', 'python', 'sql', 'ml', 'sql']
counts = Counter(words)
print(counts)
print(counts.most_common(2))
explain: Counter frequency ginta hai aur most_common se top items deta hai.
Output ko print se verify karo.
Ye Advanced Python & Performance ka basic building block hai.

examples.code:
from collections import defaultdict

groups = defaultdict(list)
for name, team in [('Asha', 'data'), ('Ravi', 'ml'), ('Meera', 'data')]:
    groups[team].append(name)
print(dict(groups))
explain: defaultdict missing key par automatic empty list deta hai, isliye if-check nahi chahiye.
Ek step aur jodne se behaviour kaise badalta hai, dekho.
Input badal kar edge case test karo.

examples.code:
from collections import deque

window = deque(maxlen=3)
readings = [10, 12, 11, 15, 14]
for value in readings:
    window.append(value)
    print(list(window), 'avg=', round(sum(window) / len(window), 1))
explain: deque(maxlen=n) purane items automatically hatata hai, isliye moving window O(1) rehta hai.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Log analysis me Counter se status codes/errors ki frequency ek line me milti hai; manual dict increments se zyada clear hai.
Bade CSV/JSON files ko generator se line-by-line process karna memory ko constant rakhta hai.
Sliding windows aur BFS me deque use hota hai kyunki dono ends par O(1) operations chahiye.

interview.q: List comprehension aur generator expression me kya chunenge?
interview.a: Ek baar use hone wale result ke liye list comprehension; bade ya streaming data ke liye generator expression, jo lazy hai aur memory nahi bharta. Generator sirf ek baar iterate hota hai.

interview.q: lru_cache kab nahi use karna chahiye?
interview.a: Jab function impure ho (I/O, time, random) ya arguments unhashable hon. Cache stale data bhi de sakta hai, isliye invalidation/ttl sochna padta hai.

interview.q: Counter aur defaultdict me kya antar hai?
interview.a: Counter counting ke liye specialised dict hai (most_common, arithmetic). defaultdict kisi bhi value ke default factory ke liye general hai.

interview.q: zip kya karta hai jab lengths alag hon?
interview.a: Sabse chhoti iterable par ruk jata hai. Strict behaviour chahiye to Python 3.10+ me `zip(a, b, strict=True)` use karo.

debugging.error: Logic error — sort() None return karta hai, list print nahi hoti
debugging.why: sort() in-place hai aur None deta hai, isliye print None dikhata hai. Ye Advanced Python & Performance ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: sorted() use karo ya pehle sort phir list print karo.
debugging.lesson: Mutating methods ka return value None hota hai — usse assign/print mat karo.

debugging.broken:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = p
print(total)
debugging.error: Logic error — total 200 aata hai, sum 300 hona chahiye
debugging.why: Assignment purani value replace karta hai; accumulator chahiye. Ye Advanced Python & Performance ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: total += p use karo ya sum(prices).
debugging.correct:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total += p
print(total)
debugging.lesson: Logic bugs exception nahi dete — chhote sample par expected value likho.

debugging.error: Logic error — pehla do items chahiye the, sirf pehla aaya
debugging.why: Slice ka end exclusive hota hai; 0:1 sirf index 0 deta hai. Ye Advanced Python & Performance ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: Slice boundaries exclusive hoti hain — range jaisa hi rule.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye Advanced Python & Performance ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.
